name: Separation pay
authority: Labor Code art.298: one month’s pay or one month per year of service, whichever is higher, on termination for installation of labour-saving devices or redundancy; art.298–299: half a month per year or one month, whichever is higher, on retrenchment, closure not due to serious losses, or disease. A fraction of at least six months counts as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Labor Code arts.298–299: one month’s pay per year of service (redundancy, the only authorised cause the exit reasons distinguish; a fraction of at least six months counts as a year), never less than one month. Tax: exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b) as pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control (redundancy or retrenchment), so the class counts toward nothing and no withholding scheme reads it.

name: Retirement pay
authority: RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): an employee retiring at 60 to 65 after at least five years’ service, with no retirement plan, is paid half a month’s salary for every year of service — 22.5 days: fifteen days, the five-day service incentive leave and one twelfth of the 13th-month pay — a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): optional retirement from sixty and compulsory at sixty-five, after five years’ service — a person retiring past sixty-five is inside it; retail, service and agricultural establishments of not more than ten workers are outside (`company.facts.small_establishment`). One-half month salary is 22.5 days of the daily rate, the daily rate being the monthly basic on the person’s own factor (365 for the monthly-paid, 313 on a six-day week, 261 on five). Tax: the statutory benefit is exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a), which is why this class pays the RA 7641 minimum only — any excess over it under a company plan would be tested against RA 4917 (age 50, ten years’ service, BIR-qualified plan).
